topic: GitHub Octoverse 2026: AI starts 40%+ of PRs. Who reviews?
caption:
More than 40% of GitHub pull requests now start with an AI agent’s first draft.

In March, that figure was 17%. By September, GitHub counted around 110 million agent-started PRs in a single month.

That’s one of the standout findings in its Octoverse 2026 report.

Another number caught my eye: 90% of agent-involved pull requests merged within two weeks in September, compared with roughly 86% without detected agent involvement.

Faster merging sounds good, but it isn’t the same thing as higher-quality code.

For developers building Shopify apps, Next.js applications, or backend services, the harder question is how we review growing volumes of AI-generated changes.

My view: keep PRs focused, require meaningful tests and security checks, and make sure a human owns the final merge decision. An agent can write the first draft. It shouldn’t replace engineering judgment.

What’s your minimum review requirement before approving an AI-written pull request?

Source: https://github.blog/news-insights/octoverse/octoverse-commits-pushes-reach-new-highs-in-2026-as-developers-build-with-agents/
